scope: Independent proposed-group and repeat review; exact full-subject record coverage checked. Ungrouped question semantics were not independently re-reviewed in this pass.

source_check_summary.render_method: PyMuPDF full source pages, local source bytes or git HEAD source bytes, SHA256 matched to review evidence. Contact sheets retain entire pages.
source_check_summary.render_warnings: Some PDFs emitted missing background XObject warnings; relevant question stems, options, code and diagrams remained visibly rendered. No question-content blocker found.

fixes.title: Repair a heap after arbitrary-node deletion
fixes.rationale: Once the target node has been located, replace it by the last complete-tree element and sift up or down to restore heap order. The 1991 question asks a deletion algorithm and complexity without explicitly stating how the target is supplied; the 2016 question explicitly supplies an array index and asks only repair cost. Keep any key-search cost separate; only the repair stage has the shared height-length bound.

question_fix.remove_from_setup: Distinguish a supplied node index from a supplied key.
question_fix.caveat: The source does not explicitly supply an index. Distinguishing a node handle from a key is reviewer analysis, not part of the printed request. O(log n) is the repair bound after locating the target; key lookup can be O(n).

fixes.title: Evaluate synthesized attributes on a parse tree

fixes.rationale: The linked subquestions share the ambiguous grammar E -> number | E+E | E*E with no precedence declarations. The first identifies the shift/reduce conflict and yacc default shift resolution; the second applies that resolution to 3*2+1 and asks precedence/associativity and value. They share conflict-resolution reasoning but are distinct exercises, not repeats.

Enumerate distinct parse trees for the supplied terminal string under the supplied grammar. The 2001 grammar S -> aSbS | bSaS | epsilon uses input abab; the 2002 arithmetic-expression grammar uses i+j*k. Different grammars and outputs are retained.

repeats.notes: Both specify max-heap level order 10,8,5,3,2, insert 1 then 7, and ask resulting level order. All given values, operations and answer choices agree apart from order.

Both use PUSH, POP and REVERSE to implement a queue, but 2000 explicitly requests ENQUEUE in one operation and DEQUEUE in three; the correct 2014 offered statement reverses those costs (ENQUEUE three, DEQUEUE one). The concrete implementation requested differs, not just answer format.

Both ask the number of two-child nodes in a binary tree from its leaf count. The 1995 question uses n leaves and degree-2 terminology with options; 2015 uses 20 leaves and a numeric blank. Same rooted-binary-tree count n-1.
Identical binary-tree setup and requested count of nodes with exactly two children; leaf count changes from 20 to 200. Both are numeric-answer questions.

Same mod-9 chained-hash simulation with one changed key (20 versus 26), but requested outputs differ: 2014 asks maximum, minimum and average chain lengths whereas 2026 asks only longest chain. Not the same requested answer, so retain as a problem pattern rather than numbers-only repeat.
Both ask minimum arbitrary pair interchanges to turn the supplied13-element level-order array into a maxheap. Only array entries and options change; neither asks heapify-operation count.
Full-page pixels 1998 page 8 and 1999 page 7 both show S->L.L|L, L->LB|B, B->0|1, 101.101=5.625, and request purely synthesized/S-attributed rules computing S.val.

limitations: Accepted groups are shared solving procedures, not equivalence claims. Keep distinct constraints and requested outputs.
